metadata.provenance: generated by adamast generate (agreement-gated, review_required at kappa 0.37) -> full-view support judging (60 traces, max_trace_chars 40000) -> trace-grounding filter (support >= 3) -> evidence-driven re-partition -> Stage-1 dry run on the 24-trace slice -> dropped Terminal_Output_Without_Verification (fired on the program's specified ending) and renumbered changed codes to fresh sequential ids -> frozen. Sub-code support provisional pending the subset re-judge. Prototyping-grade per the 2026-08-07 data amendment.

codes.name: Repetitive_Output_Loop
codes.description: Agent produces repetitive content, circularly restating the same information without progressing toward task completion.
codes.when_to_use: When output contains redundant cycles of the same content, phrases, or reasoning steps that don't advance task objectives.
codes.when_not_to_use: When repetition is intentional for emphasis or summary purposes. When agent is iterating through different items (not repeating same item).

codes.name: Downstream_Handoff_Failure
codes.description: Agent output lacks critical information, proper structure, or necessary formatting required by downstream systems (retrieval loops, parsers, or next-stage agents) to continue processing, breaking the task pipeline.
codes.when_to_use: When agent produces output that cannot be successfully consumed by the next stage of processing, whether due to missing content, structural problems, or format violations.
codes.when_not_to_use: When output is structurally valid but semantically incorrect (use B/C codes). When truncation prevents completion (use A.5 as root cause).

codes.name: Multi_Hop_Context_Degradation
codes.description: Agent loses track of information, reasoning chains, or evidence from earlier retrieval iterations as the multi-hop loop progresses, failing to maintain coherent connections across the full reasoning trajectory.
codes.when_to_use: When agent demonstrates awareness of early-stage information initially but progressively loses connection to it in later iterations of a multi-hop retrieval task.
codes.when_not_to_use: When information loss happens immediately (use A.7). When context overflow prevents initial processing (use A.2). When single-hop task shows no multi-iteration component.

codes.name: Insufficient_Retrieved_Evidence
codes.description: Environment-attributable: the passages needed to verify the claim never arrived although the gap was explicitly named in a summary and chased by well-formed, advancing queries — a corpus or retriever coverage gap, not an agent fault. DECISION TEST (apply once per evidence gap): fires only if BOTH (i) some solver summary names the missing entity — quote it — and (ii) a later query targets that entity in usable form — quote it. If (i) fails assign B.11; if (ii) fails assign B.13 or B.14. Never assign this code and B.11 to the same evidence gap.

codes.name: Coordinator_Unclear_Task_Specification
codes.description: Coordinator provides ambiguous, inconsistent, or incomplete task specifications that prevent precise execution. This includes varying instructions across invocations, ambiguous references, unclear entity boundaries, vague phrasing, or incomplete requirement statements.
codes.when_to_use: When the coordinator's task specification or claim presentation lacks the clarity needed for systematic verification
codes.when_not_to_use: When the coordinator provides clear specifications but other components fail to execute properly

codes.name: Solver_Passage_Content_Misreading
codes.description: Incorrect interpretation or misreading of factual content explicitly stated in passages. This includes claiming a passage says X when it actually says Y, misattributing information, or incorrectly extracting facts from clear text.
codes.when_to_use: When solver demonstrably misinterprets clear, explicit passage content
codes.when_not_to_use: When passage content is genuinely ambiguous or when solver makes logical inference errors (not reading errors)

codes.name: Solver_Irrelevant_Passage_Overprocessing
codes.description: Excessive analysis or reasoning about passages that are clearly irrelevant to the claim, diverting attention from relevant evidence or missing evidence gaps. Resources spent on tangential content rather than focused verification.
codes.when_to_use: When solver spends disproportionate effort analyzing clearly off-topic passages
codes.when_not_to_use: When initial relevance assessment is needed, or when passages have subtle relevance

codes.name: Evidence_Present_But_Missed
codes.description: The solver claims evidence is absent or insufficient when the retrieved passages available to it contain the needed fact. Fires only when the specific claimed-missing information is verifiably present in a passage the solver received. Does not fire when the information truly is absent from the passages (see B.11 or A.12).

codes.name: Missing_Evidence_Not_Specified
codes.description: The solver correctly recognizes the claim cannot be verified but no solver summary names the specific missing entity or fact, leaving retrieval with nothing concrete to chase. DECISION TEST (apply once per evidence gap, not per summary): scan EVERY solver summary in the trace for the missing entity named explicitly; if ANY summary names it, this code does NOT fire for that gap — assign A.12 or B.13 instead. Quote the summary text you scanned. Two codes may both fire on a trace only when they concern DIFFERENT evidence gaps.

codes.name: Verdict_Despite_Insufficiency
codes.description: A solver renders a definitive verdict (supported / refuted / factual-error) while its own analysis acknowledges the evidence is insufficient, or before verification is complete. Does not fire when the solver withholds judgment or the evidence genuinely settles the claim.

codes.name: Query_Form_Mismatch
codes.description: A coordinator retrieval query is formulated in a shape the retriever cannot use well: natural-language yes/no questions, compound multi-part asks bundling several targets, or unstructured keyword soup with no target entity. Judged on the query text alone. Does not fire for well-formed queries that merely repeat earlier ones (B.14).

codes.name: Query_Stagnation
codes.description: Successive retrieval queries fail to advance: near-identical wording across hops, re-asking already-answered questions, or ignoring gaps and guidance the summaries already provided, so later hops fetch the same or equivalent documents. Does not fire when queries change substantively between hops, even if retrieval still fails (A.12).

codes.name: Retrieval_Loop_Terminated_Early
codes.description: Fewer retrievals were executed than the task's required three: a RETRIEVAL EVENT message is absent for some hop, or a generated query was never executed. Count RETRIEVAL EVENT messages explicitly; do not infer hop counts from passage text inside prompts. Does not fire when all three retrievals executed but were unproductive (B.14).

codes.name: Broken_Multi_Hop_Chain
codes.description: Failure to maintain logical continuity across multiple inference steps, where intermediate entities or relationships are skipped or not properly connected. The reasoning jumps to a conclusion without tracing through all necessary intermediate steps.
codes.when_to_use: When the claim requires reasoning through A→B→C→D but the trace jumps from A→D without establishing B or C, or when intermediate entity connections are asserted without evidence.
codes.when_not_to_use: When all hops are attempted but evidence is missing (use C.4). Do not use for single-hop reasoning failures or when the chain is complete but contains factual errors.

codes.name: Logical_Reasoning_Error
codes.description: Solver makes logical errors in connecting evidence to claim, including invalid inferences, contradictory reasoning steps, or failure to properly chain multi-hop evidence.
codes.when_to_use: When reasoning contains logical fallacies, contradictory statements, invalid inference steps, or fails to properly construct the reasoning chain from evidence to conclusion despite having sufficient passages.
codes.when_not_to_use: When evidence is insufficient (use Solver_B.1). This is about incorrect logical processing of available evidence, not missing evidence.

codes.name: Entity_Coreference_Error
codes.description: Failure to correctly identify when different references, descriptions, or mentions refer to the same entity (under-merging), or incorrectly treating distinct entities as the same (over-merging). This includes failures in resolving pronouns, aliases, abbreviated names, descriptive references, or contextual mentions to their referent entities.
codes.when_to_use: Use when the trace shows failure to recognize that two different descriptions refer to the same entity (e.g., 'John Smith' and 'Smith' and 'he' not recognized as coreferent). Use when distinct entities are incorrectly merged (e.g., two different people with the same surname treated as one person). Use when contextual references are not resolved.
codes.when_not_to_use: Do not use for simple entity misidentification without coreference involved. Do not use for work/author confusion (use C.7). Do not use when entity boundaries are correctly identified but attributes are wrong.
